chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'I do not eat the meat of the Bukhay (a type of fish), and I do not command anyone to eat it.' In a long hadith, because his saying 'I do not eat it' is a report of his abstaining from eating it, and his saying 'I do not command' merely negates that it is something commanded. And if it were so, eating it would be obligatory, and that is not the saying of anyone. And in the report it is not stated that it is forbidden or not permissible, so it does not contradict the first report. On the basis that the prohibition of the meat of the Bukhay was something Abu al-Khattab (may God curse him) and his companions said, so it is permissible that Sulayman al-Ja'fari heard some of his companions say that and attribute it to him, so he narrated it from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) believing in his truthfulness and good belief in him, which indicates that.

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: Abu al-Khattab (a companion of the Imams)
key_terms.لُحُومَ الْبُخَايِ: Meat of the Bukhay (a type of fish)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating Bukhay fish according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the legal status of *Bukhay* meat by distinguishing between the Imam’s personal abstention (*karahat tanzih*) and a binding prohibition (*haram*). It highlights the scholarly methodology of verifying narrations, suggesting that the reported ruling was likely a companion’s inference based on the Imam’s piety rather than a definitive divine command, thus preserving the principle of permissibility (*al-asl al-ibaha*) in the absence of explicit evidence.
